_meta.indication: OPSUMIT is an endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) indicated for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group I) to delay disease progression.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven study; patients randomized to placebo, macitentan 3 mg, or macitentan 10 mg once daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with symptomatic pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group I), predominantly WHO functional class II-III; 77% female; etiologies included idiopathic/heritable and connective tissue disorder-associated PAH; about 60% on background PDE5 inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time from start of study treatment to the first morbidity or mortality event (composite primary endpoint) up to end of treatment plus 7 days, including death, atrial septostomy, lung transplantation, initiation of IV/SC prostanoids, or other worsening of PAH.
pivotal_trials.result: Macitentan 10 mg reduced the risk of the primary composite endpoint by 45% vs placebo (HR 0.55, 97.5% CI 0.39-0.76; logrank p<0.0001). Macitentan 3 mg: HR 0.704 (97.5% CL 0.516, 0.960; log rank p=0.0108). Primary endpoint events occurred in 31.4% on 10 mg vs 46.4% on placebo.

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Macitentan (ACT-064992) on Morbidity and Mortality in Patients With Symptomatic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=3% more than placebo) with OPSUMIT 10 mg vs placebo: nasopharyngitis/pharyngitis (20% vs 13%), headache (14% vs 9%), anemia (13% vs 3%), bronchitis (12% vs 6%), urinary tract infection (9% vs 6%), influenza (6% vs 2%). Key labeled risks include embryo-fetal toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and hemoglobin decrease (mean ~1.0 g/dL).
target_moa: Macitentan is an orally active, dual ETA and ETB endothelin receptor antagonist that prevents binding of ET-1 to its receptors, blocking endothelin-mediated vasoconstriction, fibrosis, proliferation, hypertrophy and inflammation in PAH.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — do not administer OPSUMIT to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm; exclude pregnancy before, monthly during, and 1 month after treatment and prevent pregnancy using acceptable contraception.

rems.type: For all females, OPSUMIT is available only through a restricted program called the OPSUMIT REMS Program because of the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified and females must comply with pregnancy testing and contraception requirements. Male patients are not enrolled.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not recommended for this application.

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use labeling based on pediatric PAH study (TOMORROW) in children with pulmonary arterial hypertension

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to labeling (Section 8.4, Pediatric Use) based on the results of Protocol #AC-055-312, titled "A multicenter, open-label, randomized study with single-arm extension period to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy of macitentan versus standard of care in children with pulmonary arterial hypertension" (TOMORROW). This sNDA was submitted in response to a pediatric Written Request under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA).

summary.text: OPSUMIT (macitentan) was approved via a standard-review NDA based on the single pivotal SERAPHIN morbidity/mortality trial; approval was subject to a REMS for teratogenicity risk and postmarketing requirements for hepatic risk surveillance. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designation was indicated.

citations.quote: The indication for this NDA is supported by a single, large, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (AC-055-302/SERAPHIN) designed to evaluate the effect of macitentan compared to placebo on morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic PAH.
In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Opsumit (macitentan) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of teratogenicity.

We have determined that an analysis of spontaneous postmarketing adverse events reported under subsection 505(k)(1) of the FDCA will not be sufficient to assess a signal of a serious risk of hepatotoxicity for Opsumit (macitentan).

requirement.text: 2093-1: A long-term prospective observational study (product exposure registry) to evaluate potential serious hepatic risks related to use of Opsumit, enrolling at least 5000 patients followed for at least 1 year.

citations.quote: 2093-1 A long-term prospective observational study (product exposure registry) to evaluate potential serious hepatic risks related to the use of Opsumit (macitentan). The registry will include a sample of patients prescribed Opsumit (macitentan) and enroll at least 5000 patients. Patients should be followed for at least 1 year.

requirement.text: 2093-2: An assessment and analysis of reports of serious hepatic adverse events in patients treated with Opsumit, with specialized follow-up and expedited reporting of hepatic events of special interest.

citations.quote: 2093-2 An assessment and analysis of reports of serious hepatic adverse events (to be defined in the protocol) in patients treated with Opsumit (macitentan) submitted according to the schedule outlined below. Specialized follow up should be obtained on these cases to collect additional information on the reports. Summary information should include the total number of cases, a summary of key facts in those cases, with pertinent expert analysis of clinically relevant information from the case series. Hepatic adverse events of special interest will require expedited reporting to the Agency.
